responseText: Source basis and boundary I used the local project sources rather than browsing more public X/article URLs, because the digest already summarizes the Alex Nguyen archive at the level needed for a clean-room blueprint. The repo’s stated goal is an Arcads-style AI UGC / AI influencer / product-to-ad system with modular graph/layer architecture, open or commodity models, and hard clean-room constraints: no code theft, no private-identity cloning, no copyrighted-video copying, and no platform-evasion tooling. README The local digest also frames Arcads as a model-router plus asset/project system, template/situation library, workflow canvas, editor/compositor, and batch UX, not as one magic model. source-digest The exposed Arcads API summary gives useful architecture clues: products, folders, projects, scripts, videos, actors, situations/templates, voices, assets, image generation, video generation, talking actors, B-roll, scene assets, presets, workflows, and webhooks. api-openapi-summary The creative-direction state is especially important here: the system should be an editable creative instrument, not a black-box talking-head generator; assets should be primitive, reusable, tagged, and provenance-tracked; and text should be rendered in post, not inside image/video models. video-creative-direction 1. Executive summary The reusable principle behind Alex’s pipelines is not “AI influencer farms” or “agents make 100M views.” The real principle is format compilation: reference inspiration→ decompose structure→ extract hook/scene/pacing/style slots→ bind persona + product + proof + CTA→ generate reusable assets→ render deterministic overlays/captions→ export drafts→ review + measure + remix The product you want is therefore not a spam bot, not an account farm, and not a one-click “make viral video” wrapper. It should be a template-driven UGC production compiler with a strong asset catalog and review queue. What is actually valuable The valuable mechanics are: Format decomposition before generation. Winning content is treated as a structure: hook type, shot rhythm, proof type, caption style, persona, visual gimmick, CTA. You clone the skeleton, not the media or identity. Persona as a production primitive. A persona is not just a face. It has belief system, voice, objections, hooks, visual taste, allowed products, forbidden claims, and consistency assets. Content pillars and hook banks. The repeatable unit is not “write a video.” It is “generate 20–50 angles per pillar, mutate hooks, bind them into templates, and test batches.” Layer separation. Images, actor video, B-roll, voice, captions, product screenshots, overlays, and export presets should be separate layers. This matches your project’s north star: graph nodes plus video-editor layers, not one-shot generation. video-creative-direction Deterministic text rendering. Never ask image/video models to draw final text. Use Canvas/Sharp/Remotion/ffmpeg for slide text, subtitles, app labels, CTAs, badges, arrows, and fake social UI. This is one of the highest-leverage rules. Model routing and caching. Cheap models for extraction, rewrite, tagging, and simple variants; stronger models for final strategy or complex visual prompting; video models only after script/assets are validated. Draft-first distribution. Scheduling/export is useful, but fully autonomous posting is the wrong product default. The safe version exports drafts, packages captions, and requires manual approval. Feedback loop. The real compounding asset is not the video output. It is the dataset of templates, hooks, personas, prompts, render settings, review scores, and downstream metrics. What is guru-noise Ignore the “100M views” framing, “AI influencer farm” bravado, arbitrary model-name hype, and platform/account operational tricks. The parts that sound like secret growth hacks usually reduce to normal direct-response creative operations: more hooks, clearer pain point, better first frame, readable captions, stronger proof, plausible persona, faster iteration, and disciplined review. The strongest product thesis: Build a safe, modular UGC format factory where every output is a draftable, inspectable, remixable graph run with provenance. 2. Implementation plan in this repo 5.1 Data model Build the first safe version around SQLite and file-backed manifests. The existing project direction already names data/asset-catalog/assets.sqlite and a schema doc target. video-creative-direction Minimum tables: SQLproducts- id- name- category- one_line_value- features_json- proof_json- claim_constraints_json- assets_json- created_at- updated_atpersonas- id- name- archetype- audience- belief_system_json- voice_rules_json- visual_rules_json- synthetic_disclosure_policy- allowed_claims_json- forbidden_claims_json- created_at- updated_atassets- id- type -- image, video, audio, caption_style, font, overlay, product_screenshot, reference- path- content_hash- prompt- provider- model- generation_params_json- provenance_json- rights_status- semantic_tags_json- vibe_tags_json- dimensions_json- duration_sec- has_alpha- loopable- caption_safe_score- persona_id- product_id- created_atformat_templates- id- name- medium- schema_version- template_yaml- source_refs_json- clean_room_notes- risk_level- status- created_athooks- id- hook_text- hook_type- template_id- persona_id- product_id- pillar_id- risk_score- performance_score- lineage_jsonscripts- id- template_id- persona_id- product_id- script_json- caption_json- safety_notes_json- statusgraph_runs- id- template_id- script_id- run_manifest_json- provider_costs_json- cache_keys_json- status- created_at- completed_atrender_outputs- id- graph_run_id- path- thumbnail_path- export_profile- duration_sec- render_manifest_json- review_statusreviews- id- object_type- object_id- reviewer- decision -- approved, rejected, needs_revision- checklist_json- notes- created_atperformance_metrics- id- render_output_id- platform- post_id- views- likes- comments- shares- saves- watch_time_avg- retention_json- ctr- conversions- imported_at Opinionated choice: do not start with a web app. Start with a strict data model, CLI, render pipeline, and local review artifacts. A UI before the graph exists will slow the architecture down. 5.2 CLI commands Use a single CLI namespace, for example ugc or arcalt. Bash# Project/catalog setupugc initugc db migrateugc asset import path/to/file --type product_screenshot --product my_appugc asset inspect asset_123# Product/persona setupugc product create products/my_app.yamlugc persona create personas/student_operator.yamlugc persona generate --product my_app --archetype creator --n 6ugc persona approve persona_001# Reference decompositionugc reference import path/to/reference.mp4 --rights structure_onlyugc format decompose ref_001 --medium ugc_video --out templates/ref_variant.yamlugc format lint templates/ref_variant.yamlugc format approve template_001# Hook/script generationugc pillars generate --product my_app --persona persona_001 --out pillars.yamlugc hooks generate --template template_001 --pillar onboarding --n 30ugc hooks mutate hook_001 --n 10ugc script generate --template template_001 --persona persona_001 --product my_app --hooks hooks.yamlugc script review script_001# Asset generationugc generate images --script script_001 --provider openai_or_jimeng --dry-runugc generate videos --script script_001 --provider kling_or_seedance --budget 10ugc generate voice --script script_001 --voice voice_001ugc captions build --script script_001# Renderingugc render slideshow --script script_001 --template template_001ugc render ugc --script script_002 --template template_ugc_talking_headugc render inspect render_001# Review/exportugc review render_001ugc export package render_001 --profile tiktok_draftugc export postiz render_001 --mode draft# Metrics/evaluationugc metrics import metrics/tiktok_export.csvugc eval hooks --product my_appugc eval templates --last 30d Important: --dry-run should be available, but the normal generation command should log cost, provider, and run manifest rather than becoming a hidden no-op. This matches the project’s tooling preference for clear, logged, credit-aware generation. video-creative-direction 5.3 Provider adapters Define provider adapters by capability, not by brand. TypeScriptinterface LlmAdapter { generateJson(prompt: Prompt, schema: JsonSchema, opts: RunOpts): Promise<JsonResult>}interface ImageAdapter { generateImage(input: ImageGenInput, opts: RunOpts): Promise<AssetRef[]>}interface VideoAdapter { generateVideo(input: VideoGenInput, opts: RunOpts): Promise<AssetRef[]>}interface TalkingActorAdapter { generateTalkingActor(input: TalkingActorInput, opts: RunOpts): Promise<AssetRef>}interface TtsAdapter { synthesize(input: TtsInput, opts: RunOpts): Promise<AssetRef>}interface SchedulerAdapter { createDraft(input: DraftInput, opts: RunOpts): Promise<DraftRef>} Capability registry: YAMLproviders: llm: cheap: use_cases: ["tagging", "hook variants", "simple rewrites"] strong: use_cases: ["format decomposition", "script critique", "safety review"] image: consistency: supports_reference_images: true use_cases: ["persona", "product context", "slide backgrounds"] fast: supports_reference_images: false use_cases: ["mood boards", "cheap backgrounds"] video: start_end_frame: use_cases: ["before_after", "transition", "motion variant"] reference_video: use_cases: ["reference-to-variant where rights allow"] talking_actor: use_cases: ["UGC presenter", "app demo narrator"] audio: tts: use_cases: ["voiceover", "dialogue"] music: use_cases: ["licensed background only"] The Arcads API summary is useful as a feature map: it exposes image generation, video generation, talking actors, B-roll, scene assets, presets, workflows, voices, and ElevenLabs credential import. api-openapi-summary Do not mirror Arcads internals. Use this as a public capability checklist. 5.4 Compositor/rendering MVP compositor: Slideshows: sharp or Canvas creates 1080×1920 PNG frames; ffmpeg concatenates frames; optional music/audio bed. UGC videos: ffmpeg stacks generated actor clips, B-roll, app screenshots, captions, product overlays, CTA cards. Captions: generated from script timing first, then manually adjustable. Text: always post-rendered. This rule is non-negotiable because the project state explicitly says not to ask video models to render readable text. video-creative-direction Better compositor: Remotion project with JSON render manifests. Template-level layout components. Safe-area validation. Subtitle collision detection. Per-platform export profiles. Side-by-side reference/similarity review. Motion templates for kinetic captions, zooms, cuts, swipe transitions, proof badges, arrows. Render manifest example: JSON{ "render_id": "render_001", "template_id": "ugc_talking_head_app_reason_v1", "script_id": "script_001", "aspect_ratio": "9:16", "resolution": [1080, 1920], "fps": 30, "layers": [ { "type": "video", "asset_id": "actor_clip_001", "start": 0, "end": 3.2, "z": 1 }, { "type": "video", "asset_id": "screen_recording_001", "start": 3.2, "end": 7.5, "z": 1 }, { "type": "caption", "text": "Stop doing this manually", "start": 0.1, "end": 2.5, "z": 10 }, { "type": "overlay", "asset_id": "cta_badge_001", "start": 11.0, "end": 14.0, "z": 11 } ], "audio": [ { "type": "voice", "asset_id": "voice_001", "start": 0 }, { "type": "music", "asset_id": "licensed_track_003", "start": 0, "gain_db": -18 } ], "provenance": { "generated_assets": ["actor_clip_001", "voice_001"], "owned_assets": ["screen_recording_001"], "human_review_required": true }} 5.5 Asset catalog Every asset should carry the answers the creative-direction doc demands: what it is, stage/layer, loopability, alpha/mask, prompt, provider, model, inspiration source, semantic tags, vibe axes, subtitle conflicts, and workflow usage. video-creative-direction MVP: Store files under data/assets/{type}/{id}.{ext}. Store metadata in SQLite. Compute content hash for caching. Track rights_status. Track review_status. Attach assets to persona_id, product_id, and template_id when relevant. Better: CLIP/embedding search. Face/persona consistency checks. Vibe scoring. Caption-safe composition scoring. Similarity checks against references. License/provenance warnings during export. 5.6 Queue Use a SQLite-backed queue before adding Redis/Celery. Tables: SQLjobs- id- job_type- input_json- status- priority- provider- idempotency_key- cache_key- cost_estimate- actual_cost- attempts- max_attempts- error- created_at- started_at- completed_at Rules: Provider concurrency defaults to 1 for expensive video generation. Every run has a budget cap. Every provider call has an idempotency key. Cache by normalized prompt + input asset hashes + model + parameters. Never enqueue direct publishing jobs. Queue draft export jobs only. Human review is a first-class job state, not an afterthought. 5.7 Evaluation loop MVP loop: Human scores each render: hook clarity, first-frame strength, caption readability, persona consistency, product clarity, claim safety, “would I post this?” Import basic metrics manually: views, watch time, likes, saves, comments, CTR, installs/conversions if available. Attribute metrics to template, hook, persona, product, CTA, caption style, and generation provider. Recommend: “make more like this,” “mutate hook,” “retire template,” “fix proof,” “reduce caption density.” Better loop: Retention curve segmentation by scene/slot. Creative fatigue detection. Bandit-style hook testing. Model-vs-human review disagreement logging. Cost-adjusted creative score: score = normalized_performance × review_quality × claim_safety × originality ÷ production_cost 6. What to ignore or explicitly not implement Do not implement these Alex-adjacent ideas/tactics: Fake geography tooling. No SIM/proxy/VPN/geotarget-account features, no device-fingerprint workflows, no “target US users from elsewhere” tooling. Account warmup automation. Treat it only as risk context. The product should support manual review, drafts, low volume, and quality, not account manipulation. Autonomous mass posting. Postiz/distro integration should create drafts or approved scheduled posts only. No “generate and blast 500 posts” mode. “AI influencer farm” as a product promise. Reframe as a compliant persona/content portfolio. The system should optimize quality and traceability, not farm behavior. Exact format/media cloning. Do not re-upload downloaded TikToks, copy exact slide text, preserve watermarks, or reconstruct a creator’s identity. Clone grammar only. Private identity cloning. No “make someone like this random creator” or “clone this person” workflow unless the person is the user or a consenting/licensed actor. Unsubstantiated transformation claims. Especially body, health, income, legal, finance, education outcomes, or “before/after” claims. Add proof requirements and review gates. Fake product proof. No fake app metrics, fake reviews, fake screenshots, fake social comments, fake “I used this and got X” testimonials. One-shot video generation as the core architecture. It is fine as a provider experiment, but it should not define the system. The project’s strength is editable layers and graph nodes. video-creative-direction AI-rendered typography. Generated visuals can contain blank screens, labels as placeholders, or non-semantic background texture. Final text belongs in the compositor. Agent branding as substance. “OpenClaw/Claude/Hermes agent” is mostly queue orchestration + prompts + file context + tool calls. Build the graph, schema, catalog, and review loop first; call it an agent later if useful. Secret-model-name chasing. Keep provider adapters swappable. Model hype expires; asset metadata, templates, and evaluation data compound. Scraping or bypass tooling. No auth challenge bypass, no rate-limit brute force, no platform risk-control bypass. Unlicensed music/meme/media dependency. Use original, licensed, user-provided, or clearly permitted assets. For meme-native styles, reproduce structure and vibe with original assets. Fully synthetic “organic” deception. Synthetic creators can be useful, but the product should not help users mislead viewers about real lived experience, endorsements, or identity. Concrete MVP build order Do this in order: Schema first: format_templates, assets, personas, products, hooks, scripts, graph_runs, reviews. Template compiler: YAML template + product/persona binding → script JSON + render manifest. Slideshow renderer: deterministic text/image compositor; fastest path to visible output. Asset catalog: import, tag, hash, provenance, rights status, review status. Hook/pillar generator: cheap LLM nodes with dedupe and safety flags. Talking-head adapter: one provider behind a capability interface; captions and overlays remain local. Draft export: local package first, Postiz draft adapter second. Review/eval loop: human review checklist + CSV metrics import. Reference decomposer: only after rights/provenance gates exist. Motion/reference-video variants: last, because this is where copyright and similarity risk spike. The product should feel like this: Create product → create persona → choose/decompose format→ generate hooks/scripts → generate/select assets→ render draft → human review → export draft→ ingest metrics → mutate the winning template That is the clean-room version of the Alex pipelines worth building.Sources
